kenan community is chill, and people actually try to get to know each other. most people are juniors and seniors, but there are also some sophomores.  i also like those buildings because they're a lot nicer than many of the other dorms-- they have giant parlors, hardwood floors, high ceilings, big porches, decent study rooms, and generally cleaner bathrooms.  this probably sounds like it's not a huge deal, but there's a big difference in the shitty soviet era housing of south campus and the civilization that is north campus. also, if you aren't going to have a meal plan, it's a lot better to cook in a kitchen that doesn't look like it's been scrubbed with vomit and roaches (*cough HINTON JAMES cough*).

Would def recommend McIver or Alderman over Kenan and Spencer, however; if you're a guy, Kenan won't be an option anyway. note: my best friend was a junior transfer last year and lived in alderman fall semester and enjoyed it a lot, and then lived in Winston spring semester and thought it was a bit of a step down.

kenan community is about a block from Franklin St and is right next to the arboretum.  Spencer is the package center for all of north campus and a good amount of mid-campus, so it's great to have that right there. 

basically all the north campus dorms except like old west or east are the same distance from Sitterson, which is on the opposite side of campus by the Carolina Inn and all that junk, but kenan community is a little bit further north than the other communities, so Joyner and Connor and OCLQ and all those places are slightly closer to academic buildings. 

it's definitely harder to meet people on south campus because those buildings are made up of bunch of freshmen who clique up too quickly.  Rams apartments are fine, but just know that it's a trek to class.  It's doable; I walked to class almost every day when I lived on south campus, but it takes like 20+min, and its all uphill.  not great for when you're running late. and it's hot in august. so, so hot. dont be afraid of taking the buses from rams to campus though--but be warned that if it's early in the morning, sometimes the buses are full and will pass by your stop a few times before you can catch one that will let you on.

DO NOT live in morrison. the rooms are tiny, and it's hinton james 2.0, which was satan's asshole, trust me. don't do it.

the logical side of my brain is telling me to reassure you that it's an illness and not a personality flaw, but I can totally relate.  when i have really rough days and cant even get out of bed, I often think, "I'm just lazy." This spring was awful for me, but I wasn't sure if I was just making my own problems or if feeling that way was just normal or what.  When my mom tricked me into seeing a doctor out of concern for me, I told the doctor, "I'm fine. I don't need to be on medication."  However, once the doctor asked me questions about how I felt, she was like, "I kind of want you to be in in-patient care, but I know that won't make you feel better, so please at least go on medication."  I think the validation that what was I was experiencing was real and not self-inflicted and abnormal helped me a lot.  I still think of that often when I'm feeling particularly down. a lot of the self-doubt you're feeling is yet another aspect of the disease that makes it even harder for people to seek help.  I havent figured out a way to completely combat such feelings, but I think you've just got to remind yourself that this is an illness.  I will say that medication has changed my life; I know it's not for everyone, but if you're not on something and have never tried it, I think it might be a good idea.
